fixes.explanation: True, baker. “Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.” (Exodus 16:21). So the bread is only there to gather until the sun gets hot. That's a deadline with no snooze button. You can't hit it once and roll over for ten more minutes, because the sun doesn't care how you slept.

Not quite, baker. The leftover manna “…became infested with maggots and began to smell.” (Exodus 16:20). That's what happened to the part they kept after Moses said not to. Moses was angry with them. In my old junk drawer, things only got dusty, so I'll take dust.

True. “So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.” (Exodus 16:24). Same overnight wait as before, and a totally different morning. Earlier, the leftovers had maggots and began to smell (Exodus 16:20). I leave one batch out and it's a mess, and they leave manna out and it's fresh. I'd like to know their secret, but I think the secret is that the LORD told them to.

problems.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
“No wind” and “Nothing blew away” assert details the passage does not give. It says the bread kept until morning developed maggots and smelled.
The explanation is flat and repetitive. It quotes that they followed Moses’ command, then repeats the same point without adding much.
